When ImageMagick fails mid-write (e.g. truncated input or corrupt EXIF), the user's original image is destroyed and the upload either fails with a confusing validation error or stores a corrupt file; there is no fallback to the original data.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The 413 error handler hardcodes 10MB regardless of which upload type failed, reporting a wrong limit in the error message. When a non-image attachment exceeds its (smaller) server limit, the user is told the limit is 10MB and retries the same file, hitting the same 413 repeatedly — misleading error with no path to resolution.
records.rationale: The diff shows the 413 handler now hardcodes `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10 MB` instead of using a setting (`Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` previously). Also the pre-upload size check similarly changes from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to a hardcoded 10MB. This makes the reported limit independent of the actual upload type/setting, so the error message can be wrong/misleading when the server rejects a different (smaller) limit.

records.rationale: In `optimized_image.rb` the diff introduces two `self.downsize` definitions back-to-back: first `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (calls `optimize("downsize", ..., "#{max_width}x#{max_height}", opts)`), then later *redefines* it as `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. Ruby will keep only the latter, so any existing/future call site passing `(from,to,width,height,opts)` will bind `dimensions=width` and `opts=height` (an Integer), which will then be used in `optimize` as `opts[:allow_animation]` and can error. records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The API download path also replaced the site-setting cap `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` with a hardcoded `10.megabytes`, so the download-size guard and the actual stored limit now come from different sources. For sites with max_image_size_kb set below 10MB, the API URL-download path will fetch images up to 10MB, then the downsize loop compresses them into range — so the effective limit for API URL uploads becomes 10MB regardless of the admin's setting, an unaccepted change in enforcement semantics; conversely no setting can raise the download cap above 10MB.

This can regress behavior for admins who configured `max_image_size_kb` > 10MB, because the download will be capped at 10MB regardless. (While `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` is still used later for post-download downsizing, the initial URL-download cap is now decoupled from the setting.)
